chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dehqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, from Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) cursed three: the one who eats his provisions alone, the one who rides in the wilderness alone, and the one who sleeps in a house alone.

key_terms.الآكل زاده وحده: The one who eats his provisions alone
key_terms.الراكب في الفلاة وحده: The one who rides in the wilderness alone
key_terms.النائم في بيت وحده: The one who sleeps in a house alone

ai.seo_question: What are the three people cursed by the Prophet for being alone?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS), linking physical isolation to spiritual vulnerability and the state of the 'cursed' (al-mal'unin). These three scenarios—eating alone, traveling alone in the wilderness, and sleeping alone—serve as practical indicators of self-sufficiency that can lead to negligence of divine remembrance or susceptibility to evil, reflecting the Shia emphasis on community and vigilance in daily conduct.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-38 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dehqan, on the authority of Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid, on the authority of Abil Hassan (MGB), “God’s Prophet (MGB)
has cursed the following three: one who eats his foodstuff alone on a trip; one who rides in the wilderness alone; and one who sleeps alone in the house.”
